findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The align-items mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment`, which is not a real CSS property in any browser engine. The declaration is invalid and silently dropped by every stylesheet parser; old-IE/legacy-Edge developers inspecting output see a phantom fallback and may rely on alignment behavior that was never applied — the mixin contains fabricated vendor support.

[ADVISORY] The flexbox() mixin emits `-moz-box`/`-moz-inline-box` old-box display values alongside the 2009 `-webkit-box` syntax but omits the matching old-box property overrides, so on any engine that honors `-moz-box` the subsequent `align-items`/`order` output (2012/standard syntax) is ignored, breaking centering on those engines. Legacy Firefox users on old-box syntax get a flex container whose align-items/order silently no-op; the header panel and small-action rows render un-centered/un-ordered with no error.

[ADVISORY] The new flex container `.contents` sets no min-width/flex-shrink policy on its text children, so a long site title that previously wrapped or clipped via float layout now overflows or truncates the flex row with no wrap handling (no flex-wrap, no overflow rule). Sites with long titles or many header widgets get a horizontally overflowing or clipped header on narrow viewports, a case the float-based layout tolerated and this diff silently drops.

[ADVISORY] `.small-action` is converted to a flex row while its two children (`.topic-avatar` and `.small-action-desc`) keep no flex sizing rules, and the old 4em left indent that separated desc from avatar is replaced by `padding: 0 1.5%`, which collapses at small widths and over-expands at wide ones. Small-action rows (e.g., 'topic closed' notices) lose their fixed avatar gutter on narrow screens, letting text crowd the avatar — an untested visual edge case with no verification in the diff.

[ADVISORY] The `align-items` mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment`, a property that exists in no browser or flexbox spec revision. Dead declaration ships into every stylesheet compiled with this mixin; harmless at runtime but misleads future contributors into believing IE-legacy support exists that the line does not actually provide.

[ADVISORY] The PR claims a performance optimization but the diff contains no verification of any kind — no benchmark, no before/after render measurement, and no test-shaped file appears anywhere in the diff, so the core acceptance criterion of the change (that flexbox is actually faster than floats here) is entirely unverified. Reviewers and future maintainers cannot distinguish a real perf win from a pure refactor, and regressions in header layout across the removed float semantics (e.g., the deleted `.title { float: left }` and `.bullet { margin-top: 5px }` compensations) have no safety net.

[BUG] The .small-action block is redesigned (flexbox conversion, padding changed from '0.5em 0 0.5em 4em' to '0 1.5%', removal of margin-top, removal of p padding-top) even though the stated intent is header layout optimization, and the new padding breaks the 4em indent that aligned .small-action-desc with the avatar column. Small-action rows (deleted posts, closed notices, custom messages in topics) lose their avatar-column indentation and vertical spacing; this is a visual regression in topic streams with no traceable requirement in 'optimize header layout performance'.

[ADVISORY] Removing the &.bullet margin-top: 5px and adding line-height: 1.5 to .extra-info-wrapper are cosmetic changes to the topic title area that are not traceable to the header performance optimization intent. Bullet-style category badges in the extra-info header shift vertically by 5px with no compensating rule added anywhere in this diff; whoever owns topic title styling gets an unrequested visual change bundled into a performance PR.

[ADVISORY] .panel is assigned @include order(3) while its flex siblings (.title, and .extra-info-wrapper which gets order(2) in topic.scss) are styled in two different files, creating hidden cross-file coupling with no order(1) ever defined. The next developer reordering or adding a header child must discover the scattered order values across header.scss and topic.scss to avoid mis-ordering; DOM-order-dependent rendering breaks silently when markup order changes because only two of the children carry explicit orders.

[ADVISORY] The align-items mixin passes $alignment verbatim into -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align, but the 2009/2011 box specs expect different keywords (start/end instead of flex-start), so the prefixed lines are dead or invalid for the alignment values this diff actually uses beyond center. The badges.css.scss call with align-items(baseline) emits -ms-flex-align: baseline, which IE10 treats as invalid and falls back to flex-start, so legacy-browser users see mis-aligned category badges; the mixin silently promises cross-browser support it does not deliver.

[ADVISORY] The PR title promises a performance optimization but the implementation is a layout-mechanism rewrite (float to flexbox) across four stylesheets including components unrelated to the header (badges.css.scss, topic-post.scss), which is scope drift rather than optimization. Reviewers and bisect tooling looking for 'optimize header performance' find a broad visual/layout refactor whose regressions (small-action spacing, badge alignment) have no acceptance criteria tied to the stated intent.

[BUG] The align-items mixin emits `-ms-align-items`, a property that does not exist in any IE version (IE10/11 use `-ms-flex-align`), so IE10+ gets no alignment at all from this line. Users on IE10/11 see header contents and .small-action rows rendered with default stretch alignment instead of center — a silently missing declaration masked by the multi-line vendor block appearing complete.

[BUG] Making `.contents` a flex container while retaining the legacy `.valign-helper` (a zero-width full-height element with a large negative bottom margin, whose entire purpose was to vertically center floated content) breaks that mechanism: inside a flex container floats are ignored and the helper becomes a flex item whose negative margin distorts line-box height instead of centering siblings. The old float-era centering hack and the new flex centering are both active on the same element, producing double/incorrect vertical alignment or clipped overflow in the header on browsers that apply both rules.

[ADVISORY] `.small-action-desc` changes from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` (left indent clearing the avatar) to `padding: 0 1.5%`, so the description text now starts under the avatar rather than beside it, and this change rides along in a PR whose stated purpose is mixin-based perf. Small-action rows (topic closed/deleted/flagged messages) visually change with no functional justification stated in the PR; reviewers auditing a 'performance' change will miss the behavioral restyle.

[ADVISORY] Hand-maintained parallel vendor mixin set (flexbox/inline-flex/align-items/order each repeating five prefixed lines) duplicates what a library like Compass/Bourbon provides, and the `order` and `align-items` mixins have already drifted (order emits `-moz-box-ordinal-group` but align-items omits the matching `-moz-box-align`, and includes the invalid `-ms-align-items`), showing the copies are not consistently maintained. The next person adding a flex mixin (e.g. justify-content) copies the drifted pattern, and each browser prefix must be fixed in every mixin separately rather than one source of truth.

[ADVISORY] The .small-action-desc padding change from '0.5em 0 0.5em 4em' plus 'margin-top: 5px' to 'padding: 0 1.5%' is a visual redesign of the small-action row, not a performance optimization, silently changing the stated objective of the PR. Users see small-action entries (deleted posts, closed topic notices, custom messages) lose their 4em left indentation that aligned the text with the avatar column and lose vertical breathing room; the PR title promises only performance work, so QA and reviewers sign off on a no-visual-change assumption and the regression ships unreviewed.

[ADVISORY] Zeroing the p margins inside .small-action-desc (margin: 5px 0 → 0) and removing the '> p { padding-top: 4px }' rule are further visual changes bundled into a change billed as a header performance optimization. Multi-paragraph custom small-action messages collapse to zero vertical spacing between paragraphs, degrading readability for forum admins who use multi-line notices; the change is invisible to anyone reviewing under the PR's stated performance-only intent.

[ADVISORY] Removing the '&.bullet { margin-top: 5px }' override on .badge-wrapper inside .extra-info-wrapper is an unexplained behavioral deletion that changes vertical alignment of bullet-style category badges, unrelated to the claimed performance goal. Forums configured with the bullet category style see category badges in the topic header sit 5px higher than the previous accepted layout, a silent visual drift outside the accepted intent of the PR.

[ADVISORY] Converting .contents to a flex container (and adding order(2)/order(3) reordering of .extra-info-wrapper and .panel) reflows every direct child of the header row, a wholesale layout change marketed under a 'performance' objective that no reviewer accepted as a visual redesign. Any child of .contents that relied on float or block layout (e.g. plugins injecting widgets like the search banner or custom header elements that appear in source order after .panel but carry no order value) now lay out in source order with order:0 against the reordered panel, producing mispositioned plugin header content that the PR's stated intent never covered.

This is a broad layout-model change that can affect any other direct children of `.contents` that are not explicitly ordered (they will default to `order: 0`), potentially changing their relative positioning vs. the newly ordered elements.
